programme.desc: Fred explores the extraordinary role of steam in the expansion of industrial Britain. Along the way, Fred learns how huge stationary steam engines continued to be used in mills, collieries and steel works until well into the 20th century.

programme.title: Matthew Bourne Remembers... Swan Lake
programme.desc: Highly acclaimed choreographer and director Sir Matthew Bourne discusses his groundbreaking reinterpretation of Swan Lake, the 1995 production that shocked the ballet world and revolutionised modern ballet by replacing the traditional female swans with a male ensemble. Thirty years and over thirty international accolades on, Bourne reflects on the challenges of reimagining a classic and the reaction at the time.

programme.title: Matthew Bourne's Swan Lake

programme.title: Earth's Seasonal Secrets
programme.desc: We celebrate the glorious nature of Summer on planet Earth, and the extraordinary ways animals and plants rise to the challenges it brings. With the sun shining and the flowers blooming, this is the season of splendid abundance, and the long hours of daylight make life burst out in a riot of activity. But you have to find clever ways to get your share of the good times while they last and as temperatures soar, everything has to deal with sweltering heat.

programme.title: Dan Cruickshank's Monuments of Remembrance
programme.desc: Dan Cruickshank reveals the extraordinary story behind the design and building of the iconic World War One cemeteries and memorials, including those at the Somme and Gallipoli, and of the remarkable man whose vision created them.

programme.sub-title: Space Mysteries: The Sky at Night Meets Curious Cases
programme.desc: Do aliens exist, and can we talk to them? What does a black hole sound like? Does the universe look like a doughnut? In a spectacular season finale, `The Sky at Night' teams up with hit podcast `Curious Cases' to answer your burning space mysteries.

programme.title: Arena
programme.sub-title: Sister Wendy and the Art of the Gospel
programme.desc: Searching of the `real' Sister Wendy Beckett, who burst on to screens in the 1990s, telling the story of Christian art and painting, but revealing little of her own extraordinary story. Wendy herself, 82, talks frankly, humorously and profoundly about her life and spirituality for the first time. Her story, inseparable from that of the Gospel, is told alongside her selection of paintings by the greatest old masters.

programme.title: Vera, Farewell Pet
programme.desc: This special documentary goes behind the scenes of the much-loved detective drama `Vera' - with exclusive access to the making of its final series - and asks why the show remains as popular as ever after 14 years and 55 feature-length episodes. Led by twice-Oscar nominated Brenda Blethyn, DCI Vera Stanhope has become a staple of British TV and the drama has charmed audiences worldwide with its complex stories, brilliant performances, and breath-taking Northumberland landscapes - while Brenda reflects on her time as Vera and talks about the camaraderie and joy of working on the show, there are also interviews with key cast members - David Leon (DS Joe Ashworth) and Jon Morrison (DC Kenny Lockhart) - the directors, the crew and author and creator of Vera Ann Cleeves. As Vera bids farewell with its final two episodes, this film celebrates its remarkable legacy and gives fans a chance to say 'farewell, pet' to one of TV's most beloved detectives.
